claims.statement: Tom Allen sold property on the south side of Geyer Avenue, between Ninth and Tenth, to Henry Steinmeyer for $2,500.
A will Tom Allen made a few weeks before his death was witnessed by Dr. Heine Marks and Dr. C. A. Newcomb.
Friends of Allen say quasi strangers are trying to get his property, taking advantage of his mental condition.
Parties were said to be trying to get possession of Allen's horse and buggy at Wand's livery stable in order to sell it.
It was reported that Allen's safety deposit box had been opened and $500 taken.
Allen's will, filed for probate, left his estate, except $20, to Mrs. Tillie Hartgrave.
Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of the estate of Thomas Allen, the late saloonkeeper and former prize fighter.
Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove (printed 'Hart', cut off) stood on the other side of the coffin at the funeral.
R. W. L. Gillespie said Allen left no estate, as was generally supposed.
Market Street believed the spirit of Tom Allen was ringing the bell behind the bar at Champion's Rest.
Hartgrove and J. W. Gillespie went to Clayton and failed to get the hat from Barrington, who denied having it.
Tillie Hartgrove, housekeeper for the late Tom Allen, says the silk hat worn by 'Lord' Barrington is the property of the Allen estate.
Barrington returned the disputed hat by messenger boy with a note reading 'From Barington'.
The hat was put on display for Allen's friends, along with the silver cup he won in 1878.
The inventory listed a champion's cup and shade, a barrel of whisky and other goods among Allen's property.
Allen's silver cup was retrieved from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938 by the father of Thomas Allen Taylor.
Tom Allen's silver cup went to Miss Hartgrove, and was retrieved from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938 by Tom Taylor's father.
In 1978 Allen's silver cup was in the home of his great-grandson Thomas Allen Taylor.
